scores.note: Hook says 'this' and hides the action. Name the action in line one. Dim-light advice is common, but the lamp rule is concrete.
The myth plus 'sink' open loop is the freshest idea in the set. Weakest line is the filler 'Small ritual, easy to repeat'. Replace it with something specific.
Names a night people dread and gives a surprising first move. Readable on mute. No change needed.
'Mistake:' openers are everywhere and the scold tone is weak. Lead with the action and the object instead.
Clear payoff (three tasks, closed notebook). 'Don't try to relax' is soft; 'Stop trying to relax. Do this instead.' sets up the payoff.
'Nobody mentions' is a stale open loop and the walk is vague. Weakest of the set.
Numbers 4 and 6 are strong. The hook is a fragment, so address the viewer directly and make it immediate.
A glass of water is a weak scroll-stopper and the link to sleep is thin. Fixing it would not beat the six kept.

final.hook: Wide awake at 1 a.m.? Stand up.
final.spoken: Wide awake at 1 a.m.? Stand up. Don't scroll. Go to another room, sit with a dim lamp and a paper book for ten minutes. Come back when your eyes feel heavy. Bed is for sleeping, not worrying. Save this for the bad nights.
visuals: bedside clock showing 1:00 in the dark
person sitting up and swinging legs out of bed
phone face down on a table
dim lamp beside an open paper book
kitchen timer set to ten minutes
person yawning and walking back to the bedroom
pillow and blanket in soft lamp light
final.why: It names a night everyone dreads and gives an unexpected first move, getting out of bed, before the viewer can scroll away.

final.hook: Stop trying to relax. Do this instead.
final.spoken: Stop trying to relax. Do this instead. Write tomorrow's three tasks on paper, then close the notebook. The list holds them, so your head doesn't have to. Two minutes, one pen. Discipline creates freedom. Save this.
visuals: person on a sofa tensely trying to relax
clenched hands loosening on a blanket
pen writing a short list in a notebook
notebook closing on a desk
notebook resting on a nightstand
pen and timer showing two minutes
calm evening desk with lamp and notebook
final.why: Telling people to stop the thing they are straining to do breaks the pattern, and 'do this instead' promises an answer within seconds.

final.hook: Overhead light off. Lamp on. 30 minutes before bed.
final.spoken: Overhead light off, lamp on, 30 minutes before bed. Your body reads bright light as daytime. Dim light tells it the day is closing. One lamp, thirty minutes, every night this week. Save this for tonight.
visuals: wall clock at 9:30 pm in a dim room
hand turning off a bright ceiling light
warm table lamp glowing in a living room
sunny window with bright daylight
sunset glow fading through curtains
single lamp on a bedside table at night
phone screen with a save icon over a cozy bedroom
final.why: The first line already contains the whole action, a time and an object, so it can be done tonight and reads without sound.

final.hook: Hand on your belly. Right now.
final.spoken: Hand on your belly, right now. Breathe in for four, out for six. Do it five times, lying in bed. Longer exhales help the body slow down. No app, no timer, just your hand. Send this to a friend who can't switch off.
visuals: hand resting on a belly under a blanket
slow exhale with soft breath visible in cool air
fingers counting four then six on a blanket
person lying in bed with eyes closed
gentle waves rolling on a quiet beach
empty nightstand with no phone or timer
two friends texting, one smiling at a phone
final.why: A physical command with 'right now' gets the viewer doing it before they decide to scroll, and the 4-in, 6-out count is easy to copy.

final.hook: Sleep doesn't start in bed. It starts at the sink.
final.spoken: Sleep doesn't start in bed. It starts at the sink. Warm water on your face, one full minute, slowly. Not for your skin. It's a signal: this day is done. Same sink, same minute, every night. Follow for more quiet evening habits.
visuals: empty made bed in soft light
bathroom sink with running water
hands splashing warm water on a face
close-up of a towel by the sink
bathroom light switched off at night
slow routine in a calm bathroom
candle and folded towel on a shelf
final.why: Two short lines contradict a common assumption and open a loop about the sink. A fixed place and time then make the habit repeatable.

final.hook: Move your phone charger across the room tonight.
final.spoken: Move your phone charger across the room tonight. Your alarm now makes you stand up, and the last scroll in bed is gone. Ten steps away is enough. Follow for small evening habits that stick.
visuals: phone glowing on a pillow in the dark
hand unplugging a charger from a wall
charger cable on a dresser far from the bed
alarm ringing on a dresser across the room
thumb scrolling a phone in bed, then put away
person walking ten steps across a bedroom
tidy bedroom with phone charging on a shelf
final.why: The first line is a concrete move with an object the viewer is probably touching right now, and the payoff arrives in the next sentence.
